title: After restart, killed Codex sessions reappear as empty phantom shells (ignore-set pruned against capped/scoped discovery scan)
outcome:
SYSTEMATIC (not a race), confirmed by delegated code review + direct inspection of the live
~/.termal/termal.sqlite. Explains BOTH user symptoms with one root cause.

MEASURED (sqlite): 661 session rows. 22 top-level Codex sessions have messages=[] , messageCount=0,
messagesLoaded=true, codexThreadState set, and preview EXACTLY "Ready to continue this Codex thread."
— the re-imported-orphan-thread marker. Their names are real prompts ("review rincon legal system",
"where are you ?", "q: I've a repro...", "can you improve the...", "resume"). Real sessions are intact
(CodexMCP=12048 msgs, LegalCodex=5830, Termal=2438). The persisted ignore set has 328 entries (was 354).

SYMPTOMS EXPLAINED:
 - "after restart I see sessions that weren't visible before" = these 22 phantoms re-appearing.
 - "I don't have the full conversation" = opening a phantom shows an EMPTY shell (0 msgs, "Ready to
   continue this Codex thread") even though it's named after a real conversation. TermAl does not
   backfill the Codex transcript on import; the phantom just looks like a lost conversation.

ROOT CAUSE (src/state_boot.rs:72-78, import_discovered_codex_threads):
   self.ignored_discovered_codex_thread_ids
       .retain(|id| discovered_thread_ids.contains(id));
 The ignore set (which suppresses killed threads from rediscovery; kill_session adds to it at
 session_lifecycle.rs:167-169, persisted in the app_state blob) is pruned to ONLY threads present in
 the CURRENT discovery scan. But that scan is (a) CAPPED at 500/home
 (src/codex_discovery.rs:29 MAX_DISCOVERED_CODEX_THREADS_PER_HOME, applied as `... order by updated_at
 desc limit 500` at codex_discovery.rs:203-218) and (b) SCOPE-filtered by workdir/projects
 (codex_discovery.rs:32-50, 250-257). So a killed thread outside the top-500-by-recency window OR
 outside the current workdir scope is absent from `threads` -> the retain DELETES its suppression entry
 and re-persists the shrunken set. On a later boot when that thread re-enters scope/recency, discovery
 finds it no longer suppressed and re-imports it as a VISIBLE top-level phantom (state_boot.rs:124-159).
 "not in the current scan" is wrongly treated as "deleted from disk."

WHY UNTESTED: killing_local_codex_session_prevents_rediscovery_after_restart
(src/tests/session_lifecycle.rs:782-829) only exercises the case where the killed thread is STILL in the
discovered list; the drop-out case (capped/scoped) is never tested.

FIX DIRECTION: prune the ignore set only against threads actually ABSENT from the underlying threads.db
(an uncapped, unscoped existence check), not against the capped/scoped `threads` result — or never
auto-prune. Add a regression test for the >500 / out-of-scope drop-out case.

Related: tm-91c (unsuppressed orphan threads from a failed thread/start — same re-import surface,
different trigger). Ruled out: hidden Claude spares (never persisted; from_inner filters !hidden at
persisted_state.rs:117) and real killed non-Codex sessions (durably tombstoned via removed_session_ids).
acceptance: Ignored IDs survive capped, scoped and empty discovery and remain suppressed when later rediscovered, including after a persisted reload.
Existing explicitly allowed or owned threads and ordinary new imports keep their behaviour, without new live-store access or an unbounded scan.
Focused regressions show the intended RED then GREEN; the independent Codex/Claude final pair has no in-scope Medium+; and the standard gate passes on the landed input.
